newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Air Force adjusts F-22 fighter program.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force adjusts F-22 fighter program.

text.p: The Air Force said Thursday it has agreed to extend development of the future F-22 stealth fighter plane for nine more months and give the development an additional $1.5 billion.
It said Air Force leaders signed an agreement with executives of Boeing Co and Lockheed Martin Corp, who are developing the plane, to make the changes.
The Air Force said some of the additional development cost would be used to "reduce identified program risk" but did not say what that is.

A spokeswoman said costs have been driven up by avionics integration, changes in the engine and "touch labor," the cost of manufacturing the plane without workers touching it and so reducing its stealthy radar-avoiding feature.
She said production schedules for the plane will also be revised but said the program's total cost of $87 billion for delivery of 438 planes by 2010 will not change.
The Air Force said the $1.5 billion will be diverted for engineering and manufacturing development of the plane from future costs. It said that development will be extended by nine months.
